## Grading

| Component | Weight | Details |
|---|---|---|
| **Labs** | 15% | 14 graded lab notebooks; your **best 12** count, at 1.25% each. Graded on assertion checks (60%), claims paragraphs (15%), reflections (25%) |
| **Homeworks** | 30% | 3 assignments × 10% — [HW1](homeworks/hw1.qmd) (due Oct 1), [HW2](homeworks/hw2.qmd) (due Oct 29), [HW3](homeworks/hw3.qmd) (due Nov 26) |
| **Midterm** | 15% | Written, Week 8 slot (Oct 15), Weeks 1–7, closed book — [logistics](exams/midterm.qmd) |
| **Project** | 20% | Team project, proposal Week 9 → midway Week 13 → report + presentation Week 15 — [details](project/index.qmd) |
| **Final** | 20% | Written, Week 15 slot (Dec 3), cumulative with Weeks 9–14 emphasis; one-sided A4 cheat sheet + calculator allowed — [logistics](exams/final.qmd) |

**Letter grades:** A ≥ 90 · B ≥ 75 · C ≥ 60 · D below 60. No curve: the
cutoffs are fixed at the start of the semester, so classmates are
collaborators, not competitors.

**Lab grading mechanics.** Labs are due before the following week's lab
session, submitted as one executed notebook on Moodle, run in **full** mode
(not SMOKE), after *Restart & run all*. Because only your best 12 of 14
count, two labs are effectively free — see the late policy below for why
this replaces lab extensions.

**Regrades.** Request within 7 days of a grade being posted, in writing,
pointing at the specific rubric line you believe was misapplied. The whole
item is regraded (the score can move either way).

## Honor code & AI policy

The course's one-sentence honor code: **submit only work you can explain.**

**AI assistants** (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and kin) are **allowed** for
labs, homeworks, and the project, under two binding conditions:

1. **Disclosure.** Every submission carries a line naming the tools used
   and for what ("Claude for debugging exercise 3's sampler; Copilot for
   plotting boilerplate"). "No AI used" is also a disclosure.
2. **Explain on request.** At any point, in office hours or after
   submission, you may be asked to explain any line of your submission —
   what it does, why it is there, what would break without it. Inability
   to explain your own submission is treated the same as undeclared use.

Undeclared AI use, or declared use you cannot explain, is an honor-code
violation: first instance zeroes the item, second goes to the university
process. The policy's intent is not to slow you down — it is to keep the
course's feedback loop honest: the asserts, claims, and reflections in
every lab are designed so that *engaging with your own outputs* is the
thing being graded, and an AI can help you get there but cannot be there
for you.

**Written exams** (midterm, final) allow **no AI and no devices**. The
midterm is closed-book; the final allows one hand-written, one-sided A4
sheet and a basic calculator, nothing else.

**Collaboration between students** follows the same explain-on-request
rule: discussing approaches is encouraged, sharing solution code is not,
and every keystroke you submit must be one you can defend alone. Project
teams share everything within the team, of course.

## Late policy

**Homeworks.** You have **three free late days** for the semester, usable
in whole-day units across HW1–HW3, no questions asked — note the use in
your submission comment. Beyond the free days, each additional day costs
10% of that homework's score, and submissions close entirely 3 days after
the deadline (solutions are discussed in labs after that).

**Labs.** No late submissions — the best-12-of-14 rule *is* the slack: a
missed week, a broken laptop, a bad fortnight are pre-forgiven twice, with
no paperwork. Spend the two freebies wisely.

**Project milestones.** The proposal (Week 9) and midway check (Week 13)
are feedback gates, not graded gates — late costs you the feedback, which
is its own penalty. The **final report and presentation (Week 15) cannot
be late**: presentations are scheduled, and reports unlock exam-week
grading; a report absent at the deadline scores what has been seen at the
midway check.

**Exams.** A missed exam with a documented university-approved excuse gets
one make-up sitting with fresh questions from the same bank; anything
else scores zero. Tell us *before* the exam when at all possible.

**The blanket clause.** Life happens — medical issues, family emergencies,
visa appointments. Write to the instructor *early*, before the deadline
when you can; early messages get accommodations, forensic reconstructions
after the fact mostly cannot.
